why: This is priority ordering: requests are served by bid (highest first) and, within a bid, by timestamp. That order is what a priority queue gives, though one sort does the same job here. Inside a bid group the round-robin means the first round alone decides who gets at least one item.
hints: You only need to know who gets zero items, not how many each customer gets. Within one bid group, what happens in the first round-robin round?

Process bid groups from highest to lowest. If the remaining inventory R is at least the group size, everyone in it gets one item in round 1. Otherwise only the first R customers by timestamp do. Then subtract min(R, sum of quantities).
Sort by (-bid, timestamp, input index), sweep over groups and mark who received something, then list the unmarked customers in input order. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Output in original input order, not in processing order.
Once inventory hits 0, every remaining lower-bid customer is unfulfilled.
A group whose total quantity exceeds R uses up all of R; one that fits passes the rest down to the next bid.
